key_insight: An AI boundary overlay supported more consistent reader interpretation of neurologic autoantibody assay images, but revisions largely followed the model’s category.
clinical_relevance: This study concerns laboratory image interpretation—not cancer drug discovery—and suggests a potential second-read aid requiring independent validation.
method: Transferred detected cell boundaries from a structural channel onto antibody-staining images.
Developed models using 2,763 records and evaluated 499 held-out records across 14 antibody targets.
Compared four readers’ classifications before and after access to the overlay and model category.
evidence_signal: The selected model achieved 85.2% agreement with a reader-derived three-class reference; recall was lowest for weak-positive or equivocal records, while reader agreement increased with assistance.
watch_item: Almost all revised ratings moved toward the model category, raising anchoring concerns; greater agreement does not establish greater diagnostic accuracy.
paper_title: AI-Assisted Interpretation of Neurologic Autoantibody Cell-Based Assays
